title: Simple animated invite lobby and named crew
scope: Owner-requested lobby revision and first M2-D presentation batch. Direct invite admission, one short name prompt, compact invite/Ready controls, avatar-attached names/ticks and visual water/hull/idle animation. Authority remains anchored until four-ready launch. Not full M2-D or production acceptance.
implemented: Invite URLs join the actual crew before collecting a new display name; remembered names avoid re-entry on reload
Server validates bounded Unicode display names and binds updates to the sender seat; reconnect retains member names; no name stored in durable checkpoint records
Own avatar says You, others show their entered names; a Ready tick appears above each ready avatar; all-four barrier and cancellation remain
Ready can be selected before all four players arrive; optional paddle instructions replace the old verbose lobby card
Water geometry, foam, idle crew and gentle hull bob/heel run on a lobby presentation clock; authoritative tick, hull pose, rowing force and save progress stay frozen
Five viewport layouts keep labels separate; normal playing view hides the lobby labels and returns to its gameplay camera
compatibility: Additive optional Crew.name snapshot field plus a validated name message; protocol5 and physics0.9 unchanged. Older clients/SDK fixtures have PaddlerN fallbacks.
corrections: Strict build rejected the generic/interleaved water attribute diagnostic; its version accessor now narrows the actual attribute type.
The initial boundary-name fixture accidentally used21 characters; the enforced20-character limit was retained and the fixture corrected.
A short landscape view exposed overlapping bow/stern labels; vertical spacing was corrected without relaxing the overlap checks.
remaining: Rest of M2-D premium boat/crew/water/audio, cliff/material and performance polish
M2-E genuine four-human/newcomer and named-device acceptance
Existing CPU/GPU/frame-time and broader production/release gates
